The comparison between the models are as follows:
| Rutherford's atomic model | Bohr's atomic model |
|---|---|
| Rutherford's atomic model is based on simple mechanics. | The main basis of Bohr's atomic model is Planck's Quantum Theory. |
| According to the Rutherford's atomic model, electrons can revolve in circular orbits of any radius about the nucleus of the atom. | According to Bohr's model of the atom, electrons rotate in a number of specific and precise energy levels instead of rotating in any arbitrary circular orbit. |
| According to electrodynamics, electrons orbiting around the nucleus will gradually lose energy. As a result, the electron moves over the nucleus in a circular path of decreasing radius. Therefore, the stability of atoms cannot be explained by Rutherford's atomic model. | According to Bohr's atomic model, electrons do not radiate any energy while rotating in a permanent orbit with fixed energy. Thus, the electron losing energy has no chance of falling into the nucleus. That is, this model is capable of predicting the stability of atoms. |
| According to this model, continuous energy radiation of electrons in atoms should result in continuous line spectrum. But in reality such a continuous line spectrum is not available. The origin of the line spectrum of atoms cannot be explained by Rutherford's model. | According to this model, energy is released by the transfer of electrons from higher energy orbits to lower energy orbits. The difference between the two energy pathways is specific. Hence the frequency of the emitted energy is also fixed and this results in the formation of the line spectrum of the atom. So, the origin of atomic line spectrum can be explained by Bohr's theory. |
| Orbital radius, electron velocity, energy and frequency of lines produced in the spectrum cannot be determined with this model. | Orbital radius, electron velocity, energy and frequency of lines produced in the spectrum can be determined with this model. |
---"}]

Explain.","marks":0,"answer":"In the electron configuration of elements, the electrons first enter the lower energy orbitals and then enter the different orbitals in order of higher energy. The energy of the orbital is determined by the value of (n+l), where n is the principal energy level and l is the sub energy level. If multiple orbitals have equal energy, the electron with lower value of n will enter that orbital first. The sub-layers are denoted by s, p, d, f whose values are 0, 1, 2, 3 respectively. Here, value of n for 4d orbital is 4 and for l, it is 2. Hence, value of (n+l) for 4d orbital is (4+2) or 6.
Again, for the 6s orbital, the value of n is 6 and the value of l is 0. Hence, the value of (n+l) is (6+0) or 6. Both these orbitals have equal energy, but the value of n in the 4d orbital is lower so the electron will enter the 4d orbital first."},{"label":"C","letter":"C","text":"Determine the atomic mass of one atom from the element ‘Y’ of the stem.","marks":0,"answer":"According to the information given in the stimulus, element “Y” is period 3 and group-17 element i.e., element Cl.

Mass of an atom of an element = ______

The molecular formulas of gas molecules formed by atoms of these elements are N₂ and Cl₂ respectively. Their diffusion rates are analyzed below.
The process of spontaneous and uniform diffusion of solid, liquid or gaseous matter in a medium is called diffusion. The lower the molecular mass of the gas, i.e. the lighter the gas, the faster it will diffuse.
Molecular mass of Cl₂ gas = (35.5 × 2) g/mol
= 71 g/mol
and Molecular mass of N₂ gas = (14 × 2) g/mol
= 28 g/mol
Therefore, the molecular mass of N₂ gas is less than the molecular mass of Cl₂ gas. That is, N₂ gas will diffuse faster than Cl₂ gas particles, which are lighter than Cl₂ gas. Since even distribution is diffusion. So diffusion rate of N₂ gas is higher than diffusion rate of Cl₂ gas.

[{"label":"A","letter":"A","text":"What is called halogen?","marks":0,"answer":"Elements that are present in group-17 of the periodic table like F, Cl, Br, I, and At are called halogen."},{"label":"B","letter":"B","text":"Explain the stability of Ar.","marks":0,"answer":"Atomic number of argon is 18. So, the electron configuration of Ar is—
Ar (18) → \(1s^22s^22p^63s^23p^6\)
From the electronic configuration Ar we can see that, there are 8 electrons present in its last shell. This means octet is complete. Due to such kind of stable electronic configuration, Ar can not donate-receive or share electrons with others. Thus, Ar exists as inert gas."},{"label":"C","letter":"C","text":"Identify the element of stem (ii).","marks":0,"answer":"According to the stem, the element has
Neutron number = 17
And actual mass of 1 atom
= \(5.357 \times 10^{-23}\) g = \(53.57 \times 10^{-24}\) g
We know, mass of 1 neutron = \(1.675 \times 10^{-24}\) g
∴ Mass of 17 neutrons
= \(17 \times 1.675 \times 10^{-24}\) g = \(28.475 \times 10^{-24}\) g
∴ Sum of the mass of protons and electrons in one atom of the element
= \((53.57 \times 10^{-24}-28.475 \times 10^{-24})\) g = \(25.095 \times 10^{-24}\) g
Since a neutral atom has same number of protons and electrons, so, let there be x number of protons or electrons in the atom of the element.
Again,
Mass of 1 proton = \(1.67 \times 10^{-24}\) g
Mass of 1 electron = \(9.11 \times 10^{-28}\) g
According to the question,
x × \(1.67 \times 10^{-24}\) + x × \(9.11 \times 10^{-28}\) = \(25.095 \times 10^{-24}\)
or, x × \(1.67 \times 10^{-24}\) + x × \(0.000911 \times 10^{-24}\)
= \(25.095 \times 10^{-24}\)
or, \(1.670911 \times 10^{-24}\) × x = \(25.095 \times 10^{-24}\)
or, x = \(\frac{25.095 \times 10^{-24}}{1.670911 \times 10^{-24}}\)
∴ x = 15
Therefore, proton number or atomic number of the element is 15.
So, the element is phosphorus."},{"label":"D","letter":"D","text":"Analyse the sequence of order of energy of stem (i) orbitals.","marks":0,"answer":"According to the (i) no. of the stem, the order of energy in the orbital is as follow — 4p < 4d< 4f.
According to the Aufbau’s principle, electron will enter the orbital with the lowest energy first and then they fill sub-shells of higher energy to create a stable electron configuration. The energy of an orbital can be calculated from the formula (n + l) where n is the principal quantum number and l is the angular momentum quantum number. The bigger the value of (n + l) is, the higher the energy of an orbital. The values of (n + l) for the orbitals of the stem are given below:
| Name of orbital | Principal Quantum Number (n) | Angular Momentum Quantum Number(l) | (n + l) value |
|---|---|---|---|
| 4f    | 4    | 3    | (4 + 3) = 7    |
| 4p    | 4    | 1    | (4 + 1) = 5    |
| 4d    | 4    | 2    | (4 + 2) = 6    |
From the values of (n + l) from the table above, it is clear that for 4p and 4d the (n + l) value is lower than 4f. Also, in case of 4f and 4d, the (n + l) value of 4f is higher and the value of 4p is the lowest. So, 4p is the lowest orbital, 4d is the second highest orbital and 4f has the highest energy orbital.
---"}]

Analyze mathematically.","marks":0,"answer":"The two gases present in the balloons are ethene and ethane respectively.
The passage of gases from a high pressure region to a low pressure region through a fine pore is called effusion. If the balloons are perforated, then the gases will come out of the hole with force. Gas pressure inside the balloon is higher than the outside. So, when the gas finds a hole to escape, it rushes towards the low pressure region, which is effusion.
Effusion depends on the molecular mass of the gas. In other words, the lighter the gas is, the quicker it will effuse.
Now,
Molar mass of ethene (C\(_2\)H\(_4\)) = 12 × 2 + 1 × 4 = 28 g
Molar mass of ethane (C\(_2\)H\(_6\)) = 12 × 2 + 1 × 6 = 30 g
As molar mass of ethene < molar mass of ethane, ethene will effuse faster. Hence, the balloon filled with ethene will burst out first.
---"}]

So, CH\(_4\) has a higher diffusion rate than CO\(_2\)."},{"label":"C","letter":"C","text":"Determine the angular momentum of the electron in the last orbit of the 'D' element of the stem.","marks":0,"answer":"There are 4 principal energy levels in the atom in figure-D of the stem. Hence, the quantum number of the last orbit will be n = 4.
From Bohr’s angular momentum formula for an electron, we get,
\[\text{mvr} = \frac{\text{nh}}{2\pi}\]
\[= \frac{4 \times 6.626 \times 10^{-34}}{2 \times 3.1416}\]
\[= 4.218 \times 10^{-34} \, \text{Js}\]
Therefore, the angular momentum of the electron present in the last orbital, that is, \(4^th\) orbital of the stem is \(4.218 \times 10^{-34} \, \text{Js}\)."},{"label":"D","letter":"D","text":"The electron configuration of the 'D' element of the stem cannot be explained by the \(2n^2\) rule-Analyze.","marks":0,"answer":"The given element of the stem is a potassium. Its number of electrons is 19 and electronic configuration is given below:
K(19) · \(1s^2 2s^2 2p^6 3s^2 3p^6 4s^1\)
The electronic configuration of this element cannot be explained using Bohr’s model or the \(2n^2\) rule. The Bohr model states that each principal energy level can contain \(2n^2\) electrons. Where ‘n’ is the number of principal energy level.
According to that rule,
Number of electrons in the \(1^{st}\) shell or K shell,
\(2n^2 = 2 \times 1^2 = 2 \text{ where } n = 1\)
Number of electrons in the \(2^{nd}\) shell or L shell
\(= 2n^2 = 2 \times 2^2 = 8 \left[ n = 2 \right]\)
Number of electrons in the \(3^{rd}\) shell or M shell
\(= 2n^2 = 2 \times 3^2 = 18 \left[ n = 3 \right]\)
Number of electrons in the \(4^{th}\) shell or N shell
\(= 2n^2 = 2 \times 4^2 = 32 \left[ n = 4 \right]\)
But here the \(19^{th}\) electron entered the \(4^{th}\) energy level instead of remaining in the \(3^{rd}\) energy level. Hence, it can be said that potassium or elements of higher atomic numbers do not follow this rule. Rather, they follow the Aufbau’s principle. According to the Aufbau’s principle, electron will enter the orbital with the lowest energy first. The energy of an orbital can be calculated from the formula \((n + l)\). If the \((n + l)\) value of two different orbitals become the same, then electron will enter that orbital which has lesser n value and electron will enter there later. According to the Aufbau principle, the order of electron entering into orbital is shown below:
According to this principle, as since the energy of 4s is less than that of 3d, the last electron entered the 4s orbital first and hence, its electronic configuration cannot be explained using the \(2n^2\) rule.

Rutherford mentioned in his atomic model that, the electrons in an atom move around the nucleus like the planets revolve around the sun in the solar system. Since the centrifugal force due to this rotation and the centripetal force due to this attraction are equal, they do not fall on the nucleus. As this model is compared to the solar system, it is called the solar model or the Solar System Atomic Model. The significance of this atomic model is explained:
i. Atoms have a central core. This core is called the nucleus. Inside the nucleus protons and outside the nucleus electrons exist. Since, the mass of an electron is negligible compared to the mass of protons and neutrons, the mass of the protons and neutrons existing inside the nucleus is considered the mass of the atom.
ii. The nucleus is very small and most of the space inside the atom is void.
iii. The number of protons present in the nucleus of an atom is equal to the number of rotating electrons around the nucleus in the energy levels. Since the charge of protons and electrons are equal and of opposite sign: therefore the overall charge of the atom is zero.
iv. The negatively charged electron feels attracted to the positively charged nucleus. This attraction force generates centripetal force and due to this centripetal force, the electrons move around the nucleus like our earth does around the sun."},{"label":"D","letter":"D","text":"Analyze the success and limitations of model A.","marks":0,"answer":"Figure-A of the stem indicates the Rutherford’s atomic model. The success and limitations of Rutherford’s atomic model as the atomic model is analysed below—
Success of Rutherford’s model:
i. The scattering of \(\alpha\)-particle experiment can be successfully explained with the help of Rutherford’s atomic model.
ii. The presence of a nucleus inside the atom can be confirmed with this model.
iii. This model has successfully confirmed and explained the neutral charge of the atom.
iv. The mass of the atom is concentrated on the nucleus of the atom.
v. Electron exists outside of the nucleus.
vi. The concept of the three-dimensional structure of an atom for the first time was given.
Limitations of Rutherford’s model:
i. The planets of the solar system are charge neutral as a whole but electrons are negatively charged.
ii. From Maxwell’s theory, we know that any charged particle, while orbiting, it will radiate energy continuously and its orbit will shrink consequently. As a result, electrons will enter the nucleus at some point. This means the atoms will be unstable. In reality, atoms do not radiate energy like this, and neither do electrons enter the nucleus.
iii. This model cannot explain the spectrum of atoms.
iv. This model did not give any idea about the structure or shape of the orbit in which electrons revolve around the nucleus.
v. This model did not discuss how the electrons revolve around the nucleus in atoms with more than one electron."}]

The octet rule refers to the tendency of atoms to prefer to have eight electrons in the valence shell. When atoms have fewer than eight electrons, they tend to react and form more stable compounds. The compounds are PCl\(_3\) and PCl\(_5\).
Electron configuration of P:
P(15) → \(1s^2 2s^2 2p^6 3s^2 3p^3\)
There are 5 valence electrons in phosphorus. It needs 3 electrons for stable electronic configuration. So, it shares 3 electrons with 3 chlorine atoms as chlorine needs only one electron to get stability.
Cl(17) → \(1s^2 2s^2 2p^6 3s^2 3p^5\)
So, P and Cl both obey octet rule in this compound PCl\(_3\).
But in case of PCl\(_5\), one electron from 3s\(^2\) goes to the 3d orbital when excited by absorbing energy. So, phosphorus contains 5 unpaired electrons. 5 electrons are shared with 5 chlorine atoms. In this case, phosphorus contains 5 + 5 = 10 electrons on its valence shell. So, it does not follow octet rule in PCl\(_5\)."}]
